articles.title: Kubernetes CI: Lease Test Mailboxes, Don't Retry Blindly
articles.summary: Email verification tests become unreliable when the mailbox is treated like an ordinary HTTP dependency. A pipeline sends a message, waits a few seconds, sees nothing, and retries. The retry may create a duplicate message, race the first delivery, or consume a mailbox that another test owns. In Kubernetes CI, the cleaner model is an inbox lease: one test run reserves one isolated mailbox for a bounded period, records that ownership, and releases it whether the test passes or fails. This turns a vague polling problem into a resource-lifecycle problem that can be operated. The failure mode: a mailbox is not a retryable dependency Most email assertions have at least four separate steps: Create or reserve a test mailbox. Trigger the application event. Wait for the message to arrive and identify the right message. Release the mailbox and retain enough evidence to debug the run. articles.summary: Book: Hexagonal Architecture in Go Also by me: Pocket Guides for Developers — the 8-book series My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for developers who ship with Claude Code and other AI coding tools Me: xgabriel.com | GitHub You put a UserRepository interface between your domain and Postgres. The review comes back with one line: "Interfaces are slow in Go. Just pass the pool." That objection is half right, and the half that is right is not the one people argue about. The dispatch itself is a pointer load and an indirect call. What costs you is that the compiler cannot see through the interface, so it stops inlining and starts sending values to the heap. That second part is a known, open compiler limitation: golang/go#36964 has tracked it since February 2020. You can check all of this yourself with one benchmark file and -gcflags=-m.
